title: Concurrent first uploads can create multiple active covers
reasoning: The handler decides whether a new cover should be active by querying for any active row, then inserting a new row with is_active=True if none exists. Two concurrent uploads against an empty cover set can both observe no active cover and both commit active rows. Later code that selects the active cover will then depend on nondeterministic row ordering.
reproduction: Issue two POST /covers/upload requests concurrently when manual_covers has no active rows; both sessions can pass the has_active check before either commits.
recommendation: Enforce the single-active-cover invariant transactionally. Prefer a database-backed constraint, such as a partial unique index for active covers where supported, plus conflict handling; otherwise serialize this critical section and re-check inside the transaction before commit.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The existing flow test uploads covers sequentially and asserts the second upload is inactive, so it cannot expose the race between two first uploads.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a concurrency test that starts two uploads against an empty database and asserts exactly one resulting cover has is_active=True.
minimumFixScope: app/api/config.py upload_manual_cover active-selection logic; ideally also ManualCover migration/schema constraint for the invariant.
